claims.text: An as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy can exhibit a fine dual-phase lamellar fcc/B2 microstructure.
The lamellar colony structure contains numerous inter-lamellar boundaries.
The internal lamellar boundaries are rigid and prone to microcrack initiation during tensile deformation.
Friction stir processing will simultaneously improve room-temperature tensile strength and ductility relative to the untreated lamellar-colony baseline.
Friction stir processing refines inter-lamellar boundaries through localized dynamic recrystallization.
Friction stir processing can be tuned to induce localized dynamic recrystallization without changing the overall fcc/B2 phase constitution.
Localized dynamic recrystallization produces refined inter-lamellar boundaries and a graded interfacial grain structure.
Friction stir processing generates severe plastic deformation together with moderate local heating.
The deformation and heating generated by FSP induce dynamic recrystallization specifically at inter-lamellar boundaries.
Interfacial refinement produces more coherent and ductile interfaces that reduce stress concentrations.
The modified interfaces hinder microcrack nucleation and promote effective load transfer.
The FSP-treated alloy will have higher yield strength and ultimate tensile strength than the untreated alloy.
The FSP-treated alloy will have greater room-temperature tensile strain to failure than the untreated alloy.
The untreated as-cast eutectic alloy has high room-temperature strength but limited ductility because its dual-phase lamellar interfaces are brittle and prone to microcracking.
The beneficial effect is limited to FSP conditions that refine interfaces without causing over-aging, coarsening, or loss of the dual-phase fcc/B2 architecture.
